name: Canadian Wildlife Habitat Conservation Stamp Program
summary: One-year grants of C$1,000 to C$150,000, matched 1:1, for conserving and restoring priority wetland and waterfowl habitat across Canada. The 2027-28 round closed on 18 October 2026.
reporting: Interim reports due mid-September and final reports due mid-March of each grant year.

eligibility.rule: Not a federal-level organization, employee, department, agency or crown corporation
Project takes place between April 1, 2027 and March 31, 2028
Project received WHC funding no more than twice previously, unless substantially changed
No endowment contributions or costs directly related to acquiring land or an interest in land
Networking project has clear learning objectives and a follow-up component
Research project includes a Canadian NAWMP Joint Venture support letter

documents: Joint Venture scientific or technical committee support letter, for research projects
Administrative office confirmation letter, for academic institution applicants

applicant_types.quote: Research, academic, and educational institutions; For profit organizations such as small businesses, companies, corporations, and industry associations; Local organizations such as community associations and groups, seniors' and youth groups, and service clubs; Provincial, territorial, municipal, and local governments and their agencies.

geography.quote: to fund conservation projects supporting NAWMP priorities across Canada.

access.quote: Eligible organizations have until October 18, 2026 to apply online via WHC's grant portal.

amount.quote: Have a funding request between $1,000 and $150,000 Canadian dollars

co_finance_required.quote: The STAMP is a matching funds program, with a required match ratio of a minimum 1:1.

reporting.quote: Reporting periods: Interim Reports due mid-September 2025 Final Reports due mid-March 2026

effort.quote: Grant applications submitted by the October 18, 2026 deadline will be reviewed by WHC Staff for eligibility.
A review panel made up of technical and professional subject matter experts will review and score each eligible application according to determined criteria.

eligibility.quote: Federal level organizations or individuals: Government employees, departments, agencies, and crown corporations.
Take place between April 1, 2027 and March 31, 2028.
Not have received WHC funding more than twice previously, unless substantial changes have been made to the project design;
WHC will not fund: Contributions to an endowment fund; Costs directly related to acquiring land or an interest in land, including a lease, conservation easement or conservation covenant;
Projects must include clear learning objectives and a follow-up component to show long-term program benefits.

Research projects require a letter of support, attached at application submission, from the scientific or technical committee of the associated North American Waterfowl Management Plan Habitat (or Species) Joint Venture in Canada.

co_finance.quote: A minimum 1:1 funding match ratio must clearly be demonstrated in the application. WHC contributions cannot exceed 50% of the project costs. Match can come from cash or in-kind contributions.

after_award.quote: Reporting Mechanism (completed at Interim and Final Reporting)
access to visit the premises or site where the activities funded under this Agreement are being carried out

documents.quote: The activity tables are used to report on project deliverables, participants and acres. It is submitted with the application, as well as with interim and final reports.

Research projects require a letter of support, attached at application submission, from the scientific or technical committee of the associated North American Waterfowl Management Plan Habitat (or Species) Joint Venture in Canada.

Provide a letter at application submission, from the administrative office confirming that the draft WHC Letter of Agreement has been reviewed, including any comments or changes that may need to be considered if the grant application is successful.
